tasks.task: Sort an inbox by urgency and draft a reply for each message

items.when: Once or twice each working day, to run the inbox in the same order every time
When a batch arrives, to read tone, urgency and warning signs before you rank it
When you need each message ranked, given a path and answered from the business's own policy
When the owner wants new emails ranked and drafted for approval on a schedule
When one message is unusual and you want a second reply in a different tone
Before a reply is approved, to check each promise in it can be kept

tasks.task: Draft replies to a batch of customer emails

items.when: When a reply depends on the order's items, payment and shipping history
When up to 30 emails need short, clear replies that stay true to policy
When each reply must quote the live order status, with refunds left for the owner's yes
When a message is a data request or a legal threat and needs a careful holding reply
When the facts are right but you want the same reply warmer, firmer or shorter
When a reply answers a complaint, to check its promises, facts and tone

tasks.task: Handle a batch of return and refund requests

items.when: When the request sits in Gorgias and you need the refund facts and policy checks in one brief
When each request must be checked against order date, item state and the rule that applies
When one request needs a clear yes, partial or no that leads with the answer
When a case is borderline and you want a second read of the policy and the refund sum
When a customer asks often, to see orders with many partial refunds before you agree
Before sending, to check refund dates and amounts promised in each reply

tasks.task: Reply to an angry customer without over-promising

items.when: When a customer is upset for the second or third time and the reply must calm and fix
When you want a second draft that names the feeling first, to compare
When the business got it wrong and owes a plain apology with what happens next
When the fix sits with someone else and needs an escalation brief and a close-out
When the apology explains, defends or asks to be forgiven instead of owning the fault
Before sending, to test the draft for promises, wrong facts and a cold tone

tasks.task: Build a library of reply templates

items.when: Before writing, to rank past tickets by the questions that come up most
When the team answers the same questions all day and needs templates with fill-in fields
When the templates should load into the help desk with a routine that drafts replies
When a template sounds canned, to try it in two or three tones and pick one
When a template answers the question but makes the customer write back to finish the job
When the set is drafted, to rank where templates drift from the tone guide

tasks.task: Write a plain returns and refunds policy

items.when: When the rules themselves are not settled: refund timing, keep-it limits and cost
When the policy is long, scattered or contradicts itself and needs one plain page
When a strict rule saves a little money but costs the goodwill the shop lives on
When the page is drafted, to find gaps and clashes with the shipping and privacy pages
When legal words crept back in and customers will not read them

tasks.task: Report monthly on returns and warranty claims

items.when: Before any sums, to find gaps, duplicates and odd values in the returns export
Once a month, to see which products and reasons drive returns and what they cost
In the first week of the month, to run the report and the policy review together
When you need return reasons counted by product to spot faults and misleading listings
When the owner asks what returns really cost, with shipping and written-off stock
When customers complain of slow refunds, to see average days and the late ones
When the client wants the monthly review to run itself and name one fix

tasks.task: Reply to a batch of warranty claims

items.when: When a claim depends on the customer's past orders, returns and notes
When each claim needs an approve, decline or send-evidence reply with the reason
When a claim ends in money back, to compare a reply that leads with the answer
Before sending, to check repair dates and replacements promised can be met

tasks.task: Write plain warranty terms and a claim form

items.when: When the business's warranty rules must become plain terms, a form and an evidence list
When customers give up on the claim form, to cut fields and test the new flow
Before publishing, to check the terms against consumer law where the business sells
When the terms read like a contract and need plain words with nothing dropped

tasks.task: Build a pack to claim costs back from a supplier

items.when: When you need the fault counted by product to show the supplier a pattern
When you need the refund rate for one product or date range to prove a bad batch
When the claim log shows one product failing and the costs must be set out for the maker

tasks.task: Decide and prepare a chargeback response

items.when: When a customer disputes a card payment and you must choose fast to accept or respond
When you know the dispute reason and need the proof to collect and where to find it
When you need the order's full payment, shipping and message history in one place

tasks.task: Plan how to clear a support backlog

items.when: When tickets piled up after a sale, a delay or time off and need an order of work
When the backlog is in email and the same run should leave rules that last
When the same few questions fill the backlog and should become help pages
When one outage or delay caused the pile and one notice could answer most of it
When the desk is Gorgias, to see which tickets are late or about to be

tasks.task: Write triage and escalation rules for the inbox

items.when: When the rules live in the owner's head and must be asked out a few questions at a time
When you need written rules for what comes first and which path each kind of message takes
When nobody knows who takes a stuck issue or when it moves up
When the desk is Gorgias and the rules need tags with reasons before any change
When the desk is Zendesk, to test the rules on the tickets waiting now

tasks.task: Write a support tone and style guide

items.when: When good past replies exist, to draw the voice out of them before writing rules
When the team needs tone by situation, word lists and side-by-side examples
When the guide needs three or four model replies that show the tone in use
When the guide exists, to test real replies against it and rank the slips

tasks.task: Write live chat opening, holding and closing scripts

items.when: When chat staff need short openers, hold lines and closers with fill-in fields
When a chat needs a flow with questions, recovery from mistakes and a handover
When an opener sounds scripted, to try it in two or three tones
When the scripts are drafted, to check they match the tone guide

tasks.task: Set up WhatsApp quick replies, greetings and order updates

items.when: When the shop is new to WhatsApp Business and needs replies, broadcasts and flows planned
When the owner answers every chat by hand and needs labelled quick replies
When order and delay updates should go out on their own with a tracking page
When broadcasts are wanted, to draft message flows with opt-in and consent rules
When chats run through Wati or Whautomate and waiting ones need reply drafts
Before a broadcast, to check the message and send plan for cost and rule flags

tasks.task: Tell customers about a price rise

items.when: Before writing, to score how ready the offer is for a rise and what to add first
When you have the old price, the new price and the reason and need the letter
When the letter is drafted, to predict the hard questions and try answers for the FAQ
Before sending, to check prices and dates agree in the letter, email and FAQ

tasks.task: Write a notice for a policy, hours or service change

items.when: When a rule changed, to find every policy page the notice must agree with
When a service stops or changes and needs a first notice, updates and an all-clear
When staff need a matching saved reply for questions the notice will cause
When you want the questions customers will ask, to shape the notice around them
Before sending, to cut the notice to what changes, when and what to do

tasks.task: Turn repeat questions into help pages and an FAQ

items.when: When several tickets ask the same thing and one short article would answer them
When one solved ticket has the full fix and should become a page with steps
When you have real questions and answers and need one findable FAQ page
Each month, to find the questions the help pages still miss and the stale ones

tasks.task: Answer where-is-my-order questions and cut them down

items.when: When a customer asks where an order is and you need its shipping history
When late-delivery messages need replies that state what is known and what happens next
When the same question floods in and updates should reach customers before they ask
Before sending, to make sure no reply promises a delivery date the carrier has not given

tasks.task: Reply to public reviews

items.when: When a batch of reviews needs a specific public reply each, with risky ones listed
When the shop also needs to know when and how to ask for reviews
When replies should be checked, risky ones held and repeat complaints flagged each batch

tasks.task: Reply to a customer who writes in another language

items.when: When a message is not in English and you need its meaning and a reply in their language
Before translating, to settle the answer from policy in plain English first
When the English source reply should be plainer so it translates cleanly

tasks.task: Review a support chatbot's missed and wrong answers

items.when: When you have recent bot chats and need missed questions and wrong answers listed
When wrong answers must be fixed against approved help text and tested again
When the bot is Intercom's and you need to know what it answers from and when it hands over

tasks.task: Report on ticket trends and repeat problems

items.when: When you have a ticket export and need themes ranked by how often they appear
When the desk is Gorgias and the owner wants the week's trends and repeat problems
Before counting, to find duplicate and merged tickets that would skew the numbers

always.when: When you are unsure of an answer, to find it in the business's docs and past tickets
Before any reply that promises a date, a refund, a credit or a fix

helpers.when: When the fix is staffing, response targets or help desk set-up, not better replies
When repeat questions need a full help centre or a product manual
When refunds, order edits or store policy pages must be changed in the store itself
When the support bot needs rebuilding, not only its wrong answers listed
When public reviews need a standing plan across review sites, not one batch of replies
When warranty terms, refunds or data requests must be checked against the law by country

gaps: No library item builds a reply template library with fill-in fields, the policy line each relies on and when not to use it
No library item covers warranty work: plain terms, evidence rules, claim replies or a claim log; only the kit does
No library item builds a supplier cost-recovery pack from a run of faulty-item claims
No library item writes triage rules that put safety, money and access first
No library item writes live chat openers, hold lines and closers, or checks a chat script
No library item writes WhatsApp Business templates in the form the app approves, or greeting and away messages by opening hours
No library item writes holiday hours, move or closure notices as one matching set for every channel
No library item writes a plain-words notice of a terms or policy change, or offers two versions of a policy page to compare
No library item sets goodwill rules: when to give a credit or gift and how much
No library item scores reply quality on a sample of sent tickets
No library item gives scripts for tricky returns such as worn items, late requests or no proof of purchase
Help desk coverage is narrow: several Gorgias items, one for Zendesk, none for Freshdesk, Help Scout or Front
